device_notes.before: 17-verse unit, one verse past the 14-16 stretch cap; disclosed rather than forced into an unsupported internal cut, as at oshb:Ezek.4.1-4.17, since no refrain-plus-fresh-onset pair stands anywhere inside 5:1-5:17 to license a shorter cut. Paseq at 5:1 and 5:7 disclosed count-only, single-witness. Marks after 5:4 (pe), 5:6, 5:7, 5:9 (samekh) and 5:10 (pe) are disclosed as intra-row, single-witness texture. An earlier ground stated here was false and is corrected: three of those five marks DO coincide with a formula onset on the verse following them. The pe after 5:4 stands before the messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.5.5, and the samekh marks after 5:6 and 5:7 stand before the messenger formulae at oshb:Ezek.5.7 and oshb:Ezek.5.8; each of those three verses is a member of the inventory's 122-verse messenger class and each carries the formula verse-initially, 5:7 behind לָכֵ֞ן (oshb:Ezek.5.7) and 5:8 behind לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Ezek.5.8). The remaining two do not: oshb:Ezek.5.10 opens on לָכֵ֗ן with no messenger formula, and oshb:Ezek.5.11 opens on the oath with the utterance signature attached mid-verse. No one of the five is read as a unit-cutting seam, but the reason is CUT-RULE and not any absence of coincidence: not one of them follows a verse that ENDS on a close-role formula, since none of 5:4, 5:6, 5:7, 5:9 or 5:10 appears in either the utterance inventory or the 64-member recognition family, and a parashah mark by itself cannot license the cut. Single witness: a pe stands after MT 4:17, the mark on record at the seam where this unit begins.

Paseq at 5:1 and 5:7 disclosed count-only, single-witness. Marks after 5:4 (pe), 5:6, 5:7, 5:9 (samekh) and 5:10 (pe) are disclosed as intra-row, single-witness texture. Three of those five marks coincide with a formula onset on the verse following them. The pe after 5:4 stands before the messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.5.5, and the samekh marks after 5:6 and 5:7 stand before the messenger formulae at oshb:Ezek.5.7 and oshb:Ezek.5.8; each of those three verses is one of the 122 verses carrying the long messenger formula, and each carries it verse-initially, 5:7 behind לָכֵ֞ן (oshb:Ezek.5.7) and 5:8 behind לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Ezek.5.8). The remaining two do not: oshb:Ezek.5.10 opens on לָכֵ֗ן with no messenger formula, and oshb:Ezek.5.11 opens on the oath with the utterance signature attached mid-verse. strongest_rejected_alternative.before: Cutting at 5:13 or 5:15, the first two 'I Yahweh have spoken' occurrences, to shorten the unit. Rejected because neither is followed by a fresh onset device - the material after each continues the same verdict speech without a messenger formula, word-event or address restarting it - so only 5:17's occurrence is unit-final. The stronger rival, weighed here under A16, is the 5:4/5:5 seam, the division the division plan holds for this chapter (the sign-act 5:1-4 set against the interpretation 5:5-17). Its near face carries a PE recorded after oshb:Ezek.5.4 and nothing further: that verse ends מִמֶּ֥נּוּ תֵצֵא אֵ֖שׁ אֶל כָּל בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, and it appears in neither the utterance inventory nor the 64-member recognition family, so it does not close on a close-role formula. Its far face is genuinely strong, oshb:Ezek.5.5 carrying the messenger formula כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה verse-initially, “The Lord Yahweh says” (web:Ezek.5.5). But CUT-RULE makes a messenger formula a sub-onset only where the addressee changes or the preceding verse has closed on a verse-final close-role formula, and neither limb holds at this seam: 5:4 addresses the prophet in the 2ms while 5:5 carries no second person at all, the shift to 2mp arriving only at 5:7 and to 2fs at 5:8; and a parashah mark cannot meet that limb by itself. The row accordingly holds the seam on those stated grounds, and the PE is recorded as corroboration of the rival and not of this unit's onset.

unchanged_prose_now.boundary_rationale: Onset: 5:1 וְאַתָּ֨ה בֶן אָדָ֜ם קַח לְךָ֣ חֶ֣רֶב חַדָּ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.5.1) (“You, son of man, take a sharp sword” (web:Ezek.5.1)), a fresh 'son of man' sub-onset distinct from 4:1's - a new symbolic object (sword/razor/hair) rather than a continuation of the siege-tile act. The messenger formula at 5:5, כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.5.5), opens the act's own interpretation rather than a competing unit (no refrain close intervenes between the hair-sign and its meaning). The oath at 5:11, חַי אָ֗נִי ('as I live'), with the utterance signature נְאֻם֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ (oshb:Ezek.5.11) attached mid-verse, marks an emphatic sub-onset of the verdict paragraph, not a unit boundary. The formula 'I, Yahweh, have spoken' recurs three times, at 5:13 (אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ (oshb:Ezek.5.13)), 5:15 (אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי (oshb:Ezek.5.15)) and 5:17 (אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי (oshb:Ezek.5.17)); the first two are paragraph-final rather than unit-final because no fresh onset device follows either (5:14 continues “Moreover I will make you a desolation” (web:Ezek.5.14) with no messenger formula or word-event reopening the address). Close: 5:17, with a pe recorded after it, before 6:1 opens with a fresh strict word-event. The verdict continues in two further 'therefore' messenger formulae addressing the same party: 5:7, לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י (oshb:Ezek.5.7) (2mp, 'therefore the Lord Yahweh says'), and 5:8, לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י (oshb:Ezek.5.8) (2fs, 'therefore the Lord Yahweh says') — both verdict paragraphs inside the same interpretation, addressing Jerusalem and the people in her as one party, with no refrain standing before either (the samekh after 5:6, 5:7 and 5:9 are disclosed as intra-row texture, not unit-cutting seams). boundary_rationale.before: Onset: oshb:Ezek.8.1 opens with the dateline וַיְהִ֣י בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשִּׁשִּׁ֗ית בַּשִּׁשִּׁי֙ בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ אֲנִי֙ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּבֵיתִ֔י וְזִקְנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה יוֹשְׁבִ֣ים לְפָנָ֑י וַתִּפֹּ֤ל עָלַי֙ שָׁ֔ם יַ֖ד אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה (sixth year, sixth month, fifth day) carrying the hand-of-YHWH idiom in its אדני יהוה form (tier-1 vision onset; the construct-only sweep counts 7 hand-of-YHWH verses book-wide, of which this is the only one carrying the double divine name), immediately followed by the transport at oshb:Ezek.8.3 וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ תַּבְנִ֣ית יָ֔ד וַיִּקָּחֵ֖נִי בְּצִיצִ֣ת רֹאשִׁ֑י וַתִּשָּׂ֣א אֹתִ֣י ר֣וּחַ בֵּֽין הָאָ֣רֶץ וּבֵ֣ין הַשָּׁמַ֡יִם וַתָּבֵא֩ אֹתִ֨י יְרוּשָׁלְַ֜מָה בְּמַרְא֣וֹת אֱלֹהִ֗ים אֶל פֶּ֜תַח שַׁ֤עַר הַפְּנִימִית֙ הַפּוֹנֶ֣ה צָפ֔וֹנָה אֲשֶׁר שָׁ֣ם מוֹשַׁ֔ב סֵ֖מֶל הַקִּנְאָ֥ה הַמַּקְנֶֽה (the Spirit lifts the prophet and sets him at Jerusalem's inner-court gate — tier-1 vision transport, sweep: 20 verses book-wide) and the phrase במראות אלהים 'in visions of God' (sweep: 3 verses book-wide — 1:1, 8:3, 40:2, the three vision-transport frames). Close: oshb:Ezek.9.11 וְהִנֵּ֞ה הָאִ֣ישׁ לְבֻ֣שׁ הַבַּדִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר הַקֶּ֨סֶת֙ בְּמָתְנָ֔יו מֵשִׁ֥יב דָּבָ֖ר לֵאמֹ֑ר עָשִׂ֕יתִי כאשר (ketiv; qere כְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר) צִוִּיתָֽנִי, “the man clothed in linen” (web:Ezek.9.11) reporting “I have done as you have commanded me.” (web:Ezek.9.11), is a narrative task-completion close; a samekh follows this same verse (single-witness), giving Masoretic corroboration exactly at the row's end. Both sides: the onset (the cry) has no formula but is a scene-change as strong as a transport verb in this vision's own idiom; the close pairs a narrative completion with a samekh, a strong Masoretic corroboration for this row's own close.

unchanged_prose_now.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.10.18 וַיֵּצֵא֙ כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֔ה מֵעַ֖ל מִפְתַּ֣ן הַבָּ֑יִת וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד עַל הַכְּרוּבִֽים resumes narrated action — כבוד יהוה goes out from the threshold and stands over the cherubim, the second stage of the glory's departure begun at 10:4. Close: oshb:Ezek.10.22 וּדְמ֣וּת פְּנֵיהֶ֔ם הֵ֣מָּה הַפָּנִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר רָאִ֨יתִי֙ עַל נְהַר כְּבָ֔ר מַרְאֵיהֶ֖ם וְאוֹתָ֑ם אִ֛ישׁ אֶל עֵ֥בֶר פָּנָ֖יו יֵלֵֽכוּ completes the 'river Chebar' identification “the faces which I saw by the river Chebar … They each went straight forward.” (web:Ezek.10.22), immediately before oshb:Ezek.11.1 opens a fresh transport (“the Spirit lifted me up and brought me to the east gate” (web:Ezek.11.1)) that continues from the very place — the east gate — where 10:19 had just stood the cherubim. Both sides: the onset is corroborated by the glory-movement device (tier-1, sweep: 9 verses); the close has no parashah mark (chapter 10 carries none) but is corroborated by the double Chebar citation at 10:20 and 10:22 and by the clean handoff to 11:1's transport verb, which is the strongest close-side evidence available in this mark-free chapter.
unchanged_prose_now.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 10:18-22 forward into 11:1-13 as one continuous east-gate scene was weighed, since 10:19 and 11:1 both name the east gate and nothing but the chapter number separates them. It was not taken because 10:18-22 completes a distinct device (the Chebar identification closing the cherubim's identity question first raised at 10:15) before 11:1's transport verb opens the courtyard scene proper with new participants (the twenty-five men, Jaazaniah, Pelatiah) who play no part in 10:18-22.
unchanged_prose_now.device_notes: Chapter 10's parashah-free status is disclosed a third and final time for this chapter's span. No K/Q, paseq or editorial note falls in 10:18-22.

unchanged_prose_now.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.11.22 וַיִּשְׂא֤וּ הַכְּרוּבִים֙ אֶת כַּנְפֵיהֶ֔ם וְהָאֽוֹפַנִּ֖ים לְעֻמָּתָ֑ם וּכְב֧וֹד אֱלֹהֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מִלְמָֽעְלָה resumes the vision frame exactly where 11:13 left it (the cherubim and wheels, last seen departing the city at 10:19). Close: oshb:Ezek.11.25 וָאֲדַבֵּ֖ר אֶל הַגּוֹלָ֑ה אֵ֛ת כָּל דִּבְרֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶרְאָֽנִי — “Then I spoke to the captives all the things that Yahweh had shown me.” (web:Ezek.11.25) — is the vision's own report-back close; a pe follows this verse (single-witness). This is the INTERNAL PARENT SEAM: oshb:Ezek.11.25 closes the transported vision that opened at 8:1, and oshb:Ezek.12.1 opens a plain word-event with no vision frame at all — the class shifts from vision report to oracle, which is why no row may run from one side of this seam to the other. Both sides: the close is double-marked (the return transport at 11:24 — “The Spirit lifted me up, and brought me in the vision by the Spirit of God into Chaldea, to the captives.” (web:Ezek.11.24) — plus the pe after 11:25); the onset of oshb:Ezek.12.1 is a bare word-event with none of the vision devices that mark this vision's earlier scenes, which is the strongest possible contrast confirming the seam.
unchanged_prose_now.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row to include oshb:Ezek.12.1 (reading the report-back and the fresh word-event as one continuous transition) was considered and rejected outright: 12:1 opens no vision device of any kind, and rows never straddle a parent seam. The four-verse length of this row is therefore not a granularity choice but the required stopping point before that seam.
unchanged_prose_now.device_notes: This row closes the P3 parent (the temple vision, oshb:Ezek.8.1-Ezek.11.25) at the seam between oshb:Ezek.11.25 and oshb:Ezek.12.1: the vision frame ends here, and oshb:Ezek.12.1 opens the P4 parent with a plain word-event carrying none of the vision's devices. This row is four verses, and the short length is disclosed as forced by the hard parent-seam stop rather than a free granularity choice. Neither a K/Q note nor a paseq stands inside this span.

A pe follows MT 19:14 (single witness), the paragraph mark standing behind this unit's onset at MT 20:1. Close: oshb:Ezek.20.26 (וָאֲטַמֵּ֤א אוֹתָם֙ בְּמַתְּנוֹתָ֔ם בְּהַעֲבִ֖יר כָּל פֶּ֣טֶר רָ֑חַם לְמַ֣עַן אֲשִׁמֵּ֔ם לְמַ֨עַן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵֽדְע֔וּ אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה) ends the third narrated generation's indictment and carries a samekh, immediately followed by a fresh therefore-plus-messenger-formula onset at oshb:Ezek.20.27. What carries the unit past the seam is the shape of the renewal: a renewed prophesying command to the same addressee, standing after a verse-final utterance signature, is a paragraph and not an onset. That renewed address already stands at web:Ezek.21.9 = oshb:Ezek.21.14, which the messenger-variant census carries as a short-form occurrence — its fourth short-form verse and its third distinct shape — so that verse is not merely a repeated addressee title, and again at web:Ezek.21.12 = oshb:Ezek.21.17, and MT 21:19 continues the same sword doubled a third time (וְתִכָּפֵ֞ל חֶ֤רֶב שְׁלִישִׁ֨תָה֙, oshb:Ezek.21.19), the sword already sharpened and polished at oshb:Ezek.21.14-16, rather than opening a new topic.

strongest_rejected_alternative.before: Cutting a fresh boundary at 24:24/24:25, where 24:24 closes with its own recognition-pattern clause (verse-final words "וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.24.24)", 2mp form with the Lord-YHWH variant, the same byte pattern observed at 23:49) before the second-person address resumes at 24:25 — rejected because 24:25-27 is the direct fulfillment of the mouth-opening promise this same sign-act ties to the prophet (24:24 explicitly links him to what precedes), no formula device (word-event, messenger formula, transport, dateline) opens at 24:25, and 24:25-27 is treated as part of the same closing movement (ending at 24:27) rather than a separate unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative.after: The rival is a cut at 24:24/24:25, and both sides of that seam carry evidence. Before it, 24:24 ends on a recognition clause of the counted adonai-form class (sweep: 5 verses), verse-final words וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.24.24), 2mp, the same form that closes 23:49, and this witness records a samekh after that verse (single-witness), which is entered as support for the rival. After it, 24:25 opens with the son-of-man address וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם (oshb:Ezek.24.25), one of the book's son-of-man verses (sweep: 93 verses), though no word-event formula, messenger formula, transport verb or dateline stands there. The cut is not taken because the sign word frames the verses that follow it: 24:24 names Ezekiel a sign, לְמוֹפֵ֔ת (oshb:Ezek.24.24), and 24:27 repeats the same word, לְמוֹפֵ֔ת (oshb:Ezek.24.27), for the prophet whose mouth will be opened, so 24:25-27 is the fulfilment the sign-act itself sets up and closes inside that inclusio rather than opening a unit of its own.

unchanged_prose_now.boundary_rationale: Onset: 25:12 opens with the messenger formula and a fresh addressee, "כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה יַ֣עַן עֲשׂ֥וֹת אֱד֛וֹם בִּנְקֹ֥ם נָקָ֖ם לְבֵ֣ית יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיֶּאְשְׁמ֥וּ אָשׁ֖וֹם וְנִקְּמ֥וּ בָהֶֽם" (oshb:Ezek.25.12) — Edom — again a messenger-formula addressee-change cut. In the WEB, “Because Edom has dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance, and has greatly offended, and taken revenge on them,” (web:Ezek.25.12). Close (both sides): 25:14 ends "וְנָתַתִּ֨י אֶת נִקְמָתִ֜י בֶּאֱד֗וֹם בְּיַד֙ עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְעָשׂ֣וּ בֶאֱד֔וֹם כְּאַפִּ֖י וְכַחֲמָתִ֑י וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ אֶת נִקְמָתִ֔י נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה" (oshb:Ezek.25.14), carrying a PE immediately after. The close itself is a disclosed deviation from the strict recognition formula: the verb clause reads "and they shall know MY VENGEANCE" (an object noun, not "that I am YHWH"), stacked with the utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH signature, "נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה" (oshb:Ezek.25.14); it belongs to the utterance list (sweep: 81 verses), not the strict recognition list (sweep: 28 verses) or either 2ms/2mp recognition family. Behind this row, 25:11 closed Moab on the strict 3mp recognition + SAMEKH; ahead, 25:15 opens a fresh messenger formula with the addressee change to the Philistines.
unchanged_prose_now.strongest_rejected_alternative: One combined 17-verse row for the whole of chapter 25 was rejected: each of the four nations closes on its own formula (2ms, 3mp, the 25:14 utterance variant, 3mp again) with its own parashah mark, and 25:12-14 is its own span; collapsing them would erase four independently marked seams for no gain in density.

unchanged_prose_now.boundary_rationale: Onset: 26:7 reopens with the messenger formula, "כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֧י מֵבִ֣יא אֶל צֹ֗ר נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֧ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֛ל מִצָּפ֖וֹן מֶ֣לֶךְ מְלָכִ֑ים בְּס֛וּס וּבְרֶ֥כֶב וּבְפָרָשִׁ֖ים וְקָהָ֥ל וְעַם רָֽב" (oshb:Ezek.26.7), introducing Nebuchadnezzar's siege by name — a fresh speech unit following the 26:6 close. In the WEB, “For the Lord Yahweh says: ‘Behold, I will bring on Tyre Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, king of kings, from the north, with horses, with chariots, with horsemen, and an army with many people.” (web:Ezek.26.7). Close (both sides): 26:14 ends "וּנְתַתִּ֞יךְ לִצְחִ֣יחַ סֶ֗לַע מִשְׁטַ֤ח חֲרָמִים֙ תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה לֹ֥א תִבָּנֶ֖ה ע֑וֹד כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ דִּבַּ֔רְתִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה" (oshb:Ezek.26.14), stacking TWO closes in one verse — "for I YHWH have spoken" (the 14-verse emphatic-close family) and the utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH signature (the 81-verse family) — with a SAMEKH immediately after; this is the strongest close-stacking in the Tyre-chapter sequence. Behind, 26:6 closed unit 1 on the recognition formula + PE; ahead, 26:15 reopens with a further fresh messenger formula shifting from direct 2fs address of Tyre's destruction to the scene of the sea-princes' reaction.
unchanged_prose_now.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through 26:18 (to approach the 7-10 verse target density) was rejected: 26:14's close is the most strongly corroborated seam in the chapter (two stacked close-formulas plus a SAMEKH), and 26:15 opens with its own messenger formula on a distinct scene (the princes' mourning), so folding it in would submerge an independently marked close.
unchanged_prose_now.device_notes: No K/Q or editorial note falls inside 26:7-14. The double close at 26:14 is disclosed as evidence weighed from the close side of this seam; the two closing families ("I YHWH have spoken", sweep: 14 verses; the utterance formula, sweep: 81 verses) are independently attested to stack at both Ezek.24.14 and Ezek.26.14.

unchanged_prose_now.boundary_rationale: Onset: 28:1 opens with the strict word-event formula, "וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.28.1). 28:2 supplies the messenger formula and the addressee, "בֶּן אָדָ֡ם אֱמֹר֩ לִנְגִ֨יד צֹ֜ר כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה יַ֣עַן גָּבַ֤הּ לִבְּךָ֙ וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֵ֣ל אָ֔נִי מוֹשַׁ֧ב אֱלֹהִ֛ים יָשַׁ֖בְתִּי בְּלֵ֣ב יַמִּ֑ים וְאַתָּ֤ה אָדָם֙ וְֽלֹא אֵ֔ל וַתִּתֵּ֥ן לִבְּךָ֖ כְּלֵ֥ב אֱלֹהִֽים" — "tell the prince [לִנְגִ֨יד (oshb:Ezek.28.2)] of Tyre" — a title the text itself distinguishes from "the king [מֶ֣לֶךְ (oshb:Ezek.28.12)] of Tyre" at 28:12, disclosed as literature-type context rather than evidence for a separate oracle. In the WEB, “Son of man, tell the prince of Tyre, ‘The Lord Yahweh says:” (web:Ezek.28.2). Close (both sides): 28:10 ends "מוֹתֵ֧י עֲרֵלִ֛ים תָּמ֖וּת בְּיַד זָרִ֑ים כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י דִבַּ֔רְתִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה" (oshb:Ezek.28.10), stacking “for I have spoken it” (web:Ezek.28.10, WEB), the i_am_yhwh_spoken family in its name-less member, with the utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH signature, with a SAMEKH immediately after. Behind, 27:36 closed the qinah chapter on parashah evidence alone; ahead, 28:11 opens a fresh strict word-event onset for the king-of-Tyre lament.
unchanged_prose_now.strongest_rejected_alternative: Classifying this row as disputation_oracle on the strength of the rhetorical "will you yet say, 'I am God'?" at 28:9 was rejected: a disputation_oracle in this book quotes a popular saying in the third person as an explicit target (e.g. 12:22, 18:2); here the boast is the prince's own claim, addressed 2ms throughout and answered with the הִנְנִ֨י (oshb:Ezek.28.7)/messenger-formula verdict pattern of an oracle_against_nation, not a cited proverb refuted.
unchanged_prose_now.device_notes: MT 28:3 disclosure: the K/Q pair records ketiv מדנאל / qere "than Daniel" (separators stripped: ketiv מדנאל / Qere מִדָּֽנִיֵּ֑אל, oshb:Ezek.28.3), and the verse ALSO carries an OSHB editorial note of the rare "adaptations to a Qere which L and BHS, by their design, do not indicate" class — one of only three such notes in the whole book (MT 14:14, 14:20, 28:3). Both are disclosed as single-witness apparatus; neither is used to argue a boundary, and the Qere itself (the Daniel comparison) is never treated as a verse-byte claim, only as the note-layer reading. 28:5 also carries a single-witness SAMEKH, internal to this row; disclosed here for symmetry with the row's close-side SAMEKH at 28:10, not argued as a competing boundary.

unchanged_prose_now.boundary_rationale: Onset: 28:25 opens with a fresh messenger formula, "כֹּֽה אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ בְּקַבְּצִ֣י אֶת בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מִן הָֽעַמִּים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָפֹ֣צוּ בָ֔ם וְנִקְדַּ֥שְׁתִּי בָ֖ם לְעֵינֵ֣י הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וְיָֽשְׁבוּ֙ עַל אַדְמָתָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לְעַבְדִּ֥י לְיַעֲקֹֽב" (oshb:Ezek.28.25), opening the gathering/restoration promise for the house of Israel; the addressee-class shift toward Israel itself began at 28:24, closing on the Adonai-form recognition variant, and 28:25 supplies this row's own formula-bounded onset. In the WEB, “When I have gathered the house of Israel from the peoples among whom they are scattered, and am shown as holy among them in the sight of the nations, then they will dwell in their own land which I gave to my servant Jacob.” (web:Ezek.28.25). Close (both sides): 28:26 ends "וְיָשְׁב֣וּ עָלֶיהָ֮ לָבֶטַח֒ וּבָנ֤וּ בָתִּים֙ וְנָטְע֣וּ כְרָמִ֔ים וְיָשְׁב֖וּ לָבֶ֑טַח בַּעֲשׂוֹתִ֣י שְׁפָטִ֗ים בְּכֹ֨ל הַשָּׁאטִ֤ים אֹתָם֙ מִסְּבִ֣יבוֹתָ֔ם וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם" (oshb:Ezek.28.26), the strict 3mp recognition formula in its fullest form ("...that I am YHWH their God"), with a SAMEKH (oshb:Ezek.28.26) immediately after. boundary_rationale.before: Onset: the witness records a pe after MT 35:15 (single-witness), at the seam this unit opens on. The sub-onset 'and you, son of man' at Ezek.36.1 וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם הִנָּבֵ֖א אֶל הָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְאָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ הָרֵי֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שִׁמְע֖וּ דְּבַר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.36.1) pivots the shared Ezek.35.1 word-event frame from Edom to “the mountains of Israel,” (web:Ezek.36.1) the second side of a two-sided unit shared with Ezek.35.1-Ezek.35.15. A cluster of six messenger-formula occurrences runs Ezek.36.2 through Ezek.36.7 (verified directly from these verses' own bytes); this cluster does not cut internally, since the addressee (the mountains) never changes and no refrain-grade close intervenes between any two occurrences. unchanged_prose_now.boundary_rationale: Onset: the strict word-event formula reopens at oshb:Ezek.37.15 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, following the pe mark recorded after oshb:Ezek.37.14 (behind this row, tier-3 single-witness, closing the unit before it) and followed at 37.16 by the commanded symbolic action (“You, son of man, take one stick” (web:Ezek.37.16)). The row runs as one unbroken masoretic paragraph internally, framed only by the pe behind it at 37.14 and the samekh closing it at 37.28, so the tradition itself treats the demonstration (37.16-20) and its spoken interpretation (37.21-28, opened by a messenger formula with no addressee change) as a single section. Close: oshb:Ezek.37.28 carries a wide-family recognition close addressed to 'the nations' rather than the strict third-person plural (this expansion sits in the wider 64-verse recognition sweep, not the strict 28-verse list) -- וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה מְקַדֵּ֖שׁ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל בִּהְי֧וֹת מִקְדָּשִׁ֛י בְּתוֹכָ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם -- with a samekh mark recorded immediately after. Both sides were weighed: the onset word-event at 37.15 is one of only 39 strict-form verses in the book, corroborated behind it by the pe at 37.14, and the samekh-marked recognition close at 37.28 is corroborated from the close side before the next word-event opens the following unit at oshb:Ezek.38.1.
